rooms.name: Acoustic Lock
rooms.description: Felt-lined doors silence the lake behind you. Inside, the beating of water is loud enough to count.

rooms.name: Test Horn
rooms.description: The mouth of the horn is polished by listeners' ears. It points toward the pilot bell.

rooms.name: Diaphragm Shop
rooms.description: Pigskin dries on hoops. Each skin is dated so the listeners know how its pitch will change with age.

rooms.name: Pulse Table
rooms.description: A needle draws the water's pulse in a bed of soot. The return stroke makes the needle jump.

rooms.name: Delay Gallery
rooms.description: The far wall has moved away on iron rollers, tuning the echo to exactly one pump stroke.

rooms.name: Pilot Bell
rooms.description: A striker has three handles for the two ends of a shift roll and the keeper who calls between them. A waiting crew needs the old signal.

encounters.cue: Call the two crews by name with the keeper’s old cadence.
encounters.result: Wren Above, Pike Below; three strokes, the middle doubled. Both crews answer. The old speaking tubes carry their names for the first time in forty years.
encounters.hint: Ask Mara at the bell landing how to call, and check both leaves of the shift roll in the archive.

changes.text: The red bead is up. Both crews have answered; the high landing can take a muster.

rooms.name: Leather Press
rooms.description: Oiled hides fold round a wooden buck in the shape of a bent ear.

rooms.name: Echo Chair
rooms.description: The chair has no back. Lean too far and the listener will miss the change in the nearest pipe.

rooms.name: Relay Hood
rooms.description: An enamel hood keeps drips off three wire contacts. A red bead shows which crew answered last.

rooms.name: Tuning Forks
rooms.description: The largest fork feels silent against the ear but shakes salt from the wall.

rooms.name: Reed Bench
rooms.description: Senn files a new brass reed while an old one rings. He stops his file on the third beat, every time.

encounters.cue: Senn the reed filer never speaks over an echo. He kept the pilot bell serviced for forty years.
encounters.result: Senn can distinguish a summons from an alarm. Use Mara’s cadence and the two muster names at the pilot bell to bring the crews to high ground.

rooms.name: Return Valve
rooms.description: A kiln-fired sleeve encloses a valve with a blank calibration dial. A drawing calls for a loaded wagon reading and a spring survey.

encounters.result: Four teeth on the salt scale against two heads at the springs: the sleeve settles and the spare conduit holds pressure. The master seat can now split its load.
encounters.hint: Find the wagon reading at the trim siding and the matching head on the three-spring survey table.

changes.text: The calibrated sleeve rests on its four-tooth stop between pulses.

rooms.name: Felt Store
rooms.description: Bundles of black felt soak up footsteps. An intruding drip sounds bigger than a thrown stone.

rooms.name: Pressure Lung
rooms.description: A leather bag inflates and collapses in its cradle. The weakest seam has been laced with silver wire.

rooms.name: Dead Chamber
rooms.description: With both doors shut a visitor hears their blood. There is a pencil tied at hand height for writing what else they hear.

rooms.name: Signal Bridge
rooms.description: Bell wires from below pass through the bridge in little ceramic eyes, one for each inhabited terrace.

rooms.name: Drop Tube
rooms.description: Messages descend in tin capsules. Scratches show which capsules were hauled back up empty.

rooms.name: Warning Comb
rooms.description: Brass teeth of different lengths pick out the knock of grit passing a dam seat.

rooms.name: Cordwalk
rooms.description: Tensioned wire stiffens the handrails. A gloved keeper could send a message without breaking stride.

rooms.name: Bypass Arch
rooms.description: Twin pipes leave the works for the springs. A dry service way follows them between the brick footings.
